\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دلال} (dallāl)}{دلال (dallāl)}]{\ur{دلال} (dallāl) — a broker; a middleman}

\label{lesson:UR-C422-dallal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a fee, then the Urdu for a currency.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دلال}}
\textbf{\ur{دلال}} — \emph{dallāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a broker; a middleman\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دلال} \ur{نے} \ur{ہمیں} \ur{ایک} \ur{مکان} \ur{دکھایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dallāl ne hameṅ ek makān dikhāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The broker showed us a house.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دلال}} (\emph{dallāl}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{dallāl}, \textquotedblleft{}a broker, one who points the way to a deal\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dallāl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dallāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dallāl ne hameṅ ek makān dikhāyā.} — The broker showed us a house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a fee, then the Urdu for a currency, then say \emph{dallāl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{دلال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A broker; a middleman\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{وصول} \ur{کرنا} (vusūl karnā)}{وصول کرنا (vusūl karnā)}]{\ur{وصول} \ur{کرنا} (vusūl karnā) — to collect (money owed); to receive}

\label{lesson:UR-C422-vusul-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for property, then the Urdu for insurance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{وصول} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{وصول} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{vusūl karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to collect (money owed); to receive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دلال} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنی} \ur{فیس} \ur{وصول} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dallāl ne apnī fīs vusūl kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The broker collected his fee.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کرایہ} \ur{وصول} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne kirāyā vusūl kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{وصول} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{vusūl karnā}) is built from \emph{vusūl}, \textquotedblleft{}receipt\textquotedblright{}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{wuṣūl}, \textquotedblleft{}arriving\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vusūl karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dallāl ne apnī fīs vusūl kī.} — The broker collected his fee.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for property, then the Urdu for insurance, then say \emph{vusūl karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لوٹانا} (lauṭānā)}{لوٹانا (lauṭānā)}]{\ur{لوٹانا} (lauṭānā) — to give back; to return (something)}

\label{lesson:UR-C422-lautana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for insurance, then the Urdu for to collect (money owed).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لوٹانا}}
\textbf{\ur{لوٹانا}} — \emph{lauṭānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to give back; to return (something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دکاندار} \ur{نے} \ur{مجھے} \ur{میرے} \ur{پیسے} \ur{لوٹائے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dukāndār ne mujhe mere paise lauṭāe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper gave me my money back.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کتاب} \ur{لوٹائی}, \emph{us ne kitāb lauṭāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لوٹانا}} (\emph{lauṭānā}) is built on \textbf{\ur{لوٹنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to come back\textquotedblright{}: this is the form for sending something back. No dictionary we use records an older form of \textbf{\ur{لوٹنا}}, so its history is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lauṭānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lauṭānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dukāndār ne mujhe mere paise lauṭāe.} — The shopkeeper gave me my money back.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for insurance, then the Urdu for to collect (money owed), then say \emph{lauṭānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{لوٹانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To give back; to return (something)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
